title: Waves and their properties
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the basic wave properties (amplitude, wavelength, period, frequency and v = fλ) or the transverse-wave-versus-sound contrast; they cover matter waves, the electromagnetic spectrum and Maxwell's theory at a Year 12 depth, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Waves and their properties
card: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the rest position. Wavelength (λ) is the distance between two matching points on neighbouring waves, such as crest to crest.
Frequency (f) is the number of waves passing a point each second, in hertz. Period (T) is the time for one wave to pass, so T = 1 ÷ f.
Wave speed, frequency and wavelength are linked by v = fλ. If the speed stays the same, a higher frequency means a shorter wavelength.

In a transverse wave, the vibration is at right angles to the direction the wave travels. Light is transverse and can travel through a vacuum. Sound is a different type of wave and needs a medium such as air.
draft.remember: v = fλ, and T = 1 ÷ f. Light needs no medium, but sound does.

a.q: A wave has a frequency of 4.0 Hz. What is its period?
a.why: Period is the time for one wave, so T = 1 ÷ 4.0 = 0.25 s. Giving 4.0 s mixes up frequency and period, which are inverses of each other.

b.q: A wave on a lake has a wavelength of 2.0 m and a frequency of 0.50 Hz. A wave of the same type then travels at the same speed with a frequency of 1.0 Hz. What is its wavelength?
b.why: The speed is v = fλ = 0.50 × 2.0 = 1.0 m/s. At 1.0 Hz, λ = 1.0 ÷ 1.0 = 1.0 m. Doubling the frequency at the same speed halves the wavelength, so 2.0 m is wrong.
b.clue: Find the speed first, then keep it fixed.
